question.text: A pivotal battle during the Pacific Theatre was this one, taking place in an atoll at the end of the Hawaiian island chain, in which American forces sank four Japanese carriers. An airport in Chicago is named for it.
question.clue: The illness of William Halsey forced Raymond Spruance to take on an unfamiliar command role in this battle, which saw SBD Dauntless Dive Bombers from the Hornet help sink the Mikuma.

swap.leadin: This country formed an army corps with Australia that fought in the Gallipoli campaign and is honored on ANZAC Day.
swap.text: Name this country, the location of silver ferns, which are featured on its airline's planes and its coat of arms. This island country, whose capital is Wellington, is located southeast of Australia.
swap.clue: The indigenous inhabitants of this country's Chatham Islands were the victims of a genocide by another indigenous group from this country, whose pa forts had been the site of intense fighting during this country's Musket Wars.

question.text: Tourists often laugh when they discover that even Hawaii has "interstate highways," something that manylearn upon landing at Daniel Inouye[ee-noh-ay]InternationalAirport in this city.
question.clue: This capital city of Hawaii. It is home to the only royal palace in the USA, Iolani Palace, as well as Waikiki Beach.

swap.leadin: Give the following the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi [why-tahn-gee].
swap.text: The treaty was written by British colonizers and purposefully mistranslated when described to leaders of this ethnic group, which didn't intend to give up all sovereignty to the British. Western contact with these people led to a period of infighting called the Musket Wars.
swap.answerHtml: Maori people (prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal, answers related to “indigenous New Zealanders”)
swap.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

question.text: Frank Bainimarama has ruled this South Pacific country since a 2006 coup. Tension between the native Melanesians and those of Indian descent makes up a significant part of this country's politics.
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.leadin: One movement of this type worships John Frum.
swap.text: Identify these religious movements, particularly prominent on Pacific Islands, in which natives assume that representatives of technologically advanced cultures must be gods due to the gifts they leave behind.
swap.clue: The Tuka movement was documented in 1885, and in 1919 G.M. Murray and F.E. Williams observed one variety of it associated with iki haveve and the Ghost Steamer, which they called Vailala Madness.

question.text: This island, the largest in Micronesia, was annexed by the United States as part of the Treaty of Paris. The Chamorro tribe occupied it before its discovery by Ferdinand Magellan in 1521.
question.clue: The 1950 Organic Act of this territory granted its residents citizenship, and a 1968 amendment of that act allowed this territory to elect a governor.

swap.leadin: This modern-day nation was the site of the Tu'i empire, which saw a period of mass expansion under its emperor Momo.
swap.text: Name this Polynesian island nation. Its King Tupou VI resides in the Royal Palace at Nuku'alofa.
swap.clue: Many examples of dance-poems called lakalaka were composed by this country's 20th century queen Salote.

question.leadin: This treaty was the subject of R v. Symonds and another case brought by political leader Wi Parata.
question.text: Identify this treaty partially crafted by James Freeman and William Hobson and subject to several objections by the local rangatira and cannibalism enthusiast, Moka Kainga-mataa.
question.clue: Instructions for this treaty were issued by Lord Normanby, and it was drafted in four days by James Busby and Lieutenant Governor William Hobson.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the early exploration of Australia and New Zealand.
swap.text: The first Europeans to sight New Zealand were in this man's crew. After members of his crew were killed by the Maori in Golden Bay in 1642, this Dutch explorer renamed the bay to Murderer's Bay.
swap.clue: This Dutch explorer who mapped much of Australia in addition to discovering Fiji and other Pacific Islands

question.leadin: The women's Mau movement emerged to oppose colonial rule in this country after the Black Saturday massacre.
question.text: Name this Polynesian country where the Mau movement opposed New Zealand's colonial rule in the late 1920s and early 1930s. This country was colonized after German-backed rebels were defeated in the Siege of Apia.
question.answerHtml: Independent State of Samoa [accept Western Samoa; do NOT accept or prompt on “American Samoa”]

swap.text: Due to a similar story, seven of these figures at Ahu Akivi are thought to depict seven scouts who discovered Rapa Nui. Those examples of these figures are the only ones on Rapa Nui to face the ocean.
swap.answerHtml: moai [prompt on Easter Island heads or Easter Island statues]
swap.clue: A system of ropes likely allowed these objects to "walk" from Rano Raraku to ahu platforms.

question.leadin: A faction of this party known as the "Backbone club" split off to form the ACT party.
question.text: Name this party which floated its country's currency and introduced market reforms as part of Minister of Finance Roger Douglas's "Rogernomics." This party opposes the National Party.
question.answerHtml: New Zealand Labour Party [accept equivalents; prompt on Labour by asking “in what country?”]

swap.leadin: The expansion of these people were theorized in the "entangled bank" and "express train" models.
swap.text: Name these Austronesian people who settled Pacific Islands like Easter Island and Hawaii. These people settled further east, unlike the Melanesians and Micronesians.
swap.clue: The range of the non-native sweet potato in places settled by these people supports genetic evidence of contact with Pre-Columbia Americans.

question.text: After the mutiny, Queiros's crew took his ship to Acapulco, leaving this second-in-command to sail the rest of the fleet to Manila. This man may have sighted Australia during that voyage through a strait now named for him.

swap.leadin: A leader of this expedition beat Charles Gray after Gray stole skilligolee (SKIL-ee-goh-lee) porridge and contracted dysentery.
swap.text: Name this failed 1860s expedition which is commemorated on the Dig Tree. The Irish soldier John King was the only man to successfully see this expedition to fruition.
swap.answerHtml: Burke and Wills expedition [or answers describing the expedition of Robert O'Hara Burke and William John Wills; or Victorian Exploring Expedition]

question.text: The US Navy's victory at the Battle of the Coral Sea foiled this Japanese operation, whose goal was to capture Port Moresby in New Guinea and set the stage for an invasion of Australia.

swap.leadin: An airbase called Henderson Field was a critical facility on this island, where ships coming in from the northwest were often sunk in "The Slot," or Ironbottom Sound.
swap.text: Name this island, where U.S. and Japanese forces fought as the year 1942 gave way to 1943.
swap.clue: The naval battle named for this island in the Solomon Islands occurred after the United States captured Henderson Airfield. The early battles on this island had the codename Operation Watchtower, and it was the first major offensive by the Allies against Japan.

question.leadin: This man's premiership began after he ousted Laisenia Qarase in a 2006 coup.
question.text: Identify this naval commodore who served as Prime Minister of Fiji for 18 years. This man forced President Kaimese Mara to resign in 2000 during a so-called "coup within a coup" while Prime Minister Mahendra Chaudry and his cabinet were being held hostage by George Speight.

swap.leadin: Native speakers of this language started to use the word palapala in the 1820s to refer to the body of written knowledge produced with the help of Christian missionaries.
swap.text: Name this language. The nineteenth-century historians Davida Malo and "Kepelino" both wrote in this language, and Lorrin A. Thurston wrote a constitution in this language.
